description: Above Kitch — Permanent Recipe Library. Add new recipes each week. Never delete — use 'retired: true' to remove from rotation.

recipes.name: Strawberry Lemon Protein Yogurt Bowl
recipes.equipment: 4 meal prep containers, small zip bags
instructions: Add Greek yogurt to meal prep container. Add protein powder.
Whisk together until completely smooth — no dry powder clumps.
Seal container. Store strawberries in a small zip bag on top.
Morning-of: dump berries into yogurt, stir gently. Add granola on top.
Austin: drizzle almond butter + honey. Add lemon zest if using.
Optional: mash a few strawberries into the yogurt base for a jam swirl.
recipes.batch_note: Whisk yogurt + protein Sunday. Bag strawberries separately — add granola + berries morning-of so nothing goes soggy. Lasts 5 days refrigerated.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: use 3/4 cup yogurt, skip almond butter. Add 1/4 avocado on the side if she wants healthy fat.
recipes.seasonal_note: Pittsburgh strawberries start arriving late April from the Strip District — sweeter and more fragrant than grocery store.

ratings.notes: Solid breakfast. Rhubarb version coming this week should be even better.

recipes.name: Turkey Sausage & Spring Onion Egg Muffins
recipes.equipment: 12-cup muffin tin, large mixing bowl, whisk
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin well.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs and egg whites until fully combined.
Fold in turkey sausage, spinach, spring onions, feta, garlic powder, pepper flakes, salt and pepper.
Pour evenly into muffin cups — fill each about 3/4 full.
Bake 18-20 min until puffed and set in the center.
Cool in tin 5 min, then transfer to wire rack. Cool fully before storing.
Store airtight in fridge. Reheat before eating.
recipes.batch_note: Bake all 12 Sunday. Cool completely before storing airtight. Reheat in Breville at 325°F for 8 min or microwave 60 sec. Last 5 days refrigerated.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron gets 3 muffins. Add 1/4 sliced avocado on the side morning-of.
recipes.seasonal_note: Spring onions just coming into season in PA — their mild grassy bite lifts egg muffins out of generic territory. Use the whole stalk.

ratings.notes: Good but asparagus bites this week should be an upgrade.

recipes.name: Lemon Herb Chicken Mediterranean Bowl
recipes.equipment: 2 meal prep containers per person, small dressing jar

macro_strings.cameron: 505 cal | 35g P | 15g F | 47g C  (+60 cal, 3g F for 1/4 avocado)

ingredients.name: Lemon herb batch chicken thighs, sliced

instructions: Whisk together all dressing ingredients. Taste and adjust lemon/salt. Store in a small jar.
Build bowl: arugula base, then quinoa, chicken, tomatoes, cucumber, red onion.
Top with feta and olives.
Seal dressing separately. Drizzle over bowl day-of and toss before eating.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado, sliced, on top day-of.
recipes.batch_note: Assemble 2 containers per person Sunday. Dressing stays separate in a small jar — drizzle day-of. Lasts 3 days refrigerated.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado fresh daily. An extra drizzle of lemon never hurts.
recipes.seasonal_note: Arugula is at peak spring peppery brightness right now. This bowl is the whole point of April in Pittsburgh.

recipes.name: Sesame Ginger Chicken & Edamame Bowl
recipes.equipment: 2 meal prep containers per person, small dressing jar

macro_strings.cameron: 515 cal | 36g P | 13g F | 52g C  (+60 cal for 1/4 avocado)

ingredients.name: Batch chicken thighs, sliced or shredded

instructions: Whisk all dressing ingredients. Adjust soy for salt, rice vinegar for brightness.
Thaw edamame under warm water or microwave 2 min.
Build bowl: rice base, chicken, edamame, spinach, spring onions.
Top with sesame seeds and shredded radish if using.
Seal dressing separately. Pour over day-of, toss well.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado, drizzle extra sesame oil.
recipes.batch_note: Assemble 2 containers per person Sunday. Keep sesame dressing separate — it holds 5 days.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado and extra drizzle of sesame oil. Bold sauce, lighter on the Sriracha.
recipes.seasonal_note: Spring onions make the difference here — don't substitute with regular scallions from months ago.

ratings.notes: Austin liked it, Cameron found it a bit monotonous by Thursday.

recipes.name: Pesto Chicken & Spring Pea Quinoa Salad
recipes.equipment: 2 meal prep containers per person

macro_strings.cameron: 510 cal | 35g P | 18g F | 38g C  (+60 cal for 1/4 avocado)

instructions: Toss cooled quinoa with pesto until fully coated — this is the dressing.
Combine arugula, cherry tomatoes, peas, and pesto quinoa in a bowl.
Add sliced chicken on top.
Finish with parmesan, a squeeze of lemon, and cracked black pepper.
Pack into containers — arugula is sturdy enough to hold dressed.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado, sliced, day-of. Squeeze extra lemon over avocado.
recipes.batch_note: Assemble Fri morning or Thu evening. Toss quinoa with pesto first — it IS the dressing. No extra oil needed. Keeps 2 days.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado. Thin pesto with 1 tbsp lemon juice if she wants it creamier.
recipes.seasonal_note: Fresh spring peas raw here — their snap and sweetness beats cooked.

ratings.notes: Great Fri/Sat lunch. The spring peas made it.

recipes.name: Greek Chicken Arugula Salad with Feta & Lemon Vinaigrette
recipes.equipment: Salad bowl or meal prep container, small jar

macro_strings.cameron: 505 cal | 35g P | 16g F | 35g C  (+60 cal for 1/4 avocado)

instructions: Whisk together lemon vinaigrette.
Build salad: arugula, quinoa, tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, olives.
Lay chicken on top. Add feta and fresh dill.
Store vinaigrette separately. Dress right before eating.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado, extra feta, extra dill.
recipes.batch_note: Assemble Saturday evening. This uses the last of the batch chicken. Light, fast Sunday lunch.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado and extra feta.
recipes.seasonal_note: Dill is the secret — its brightness ties lemon and feta together.

ratings.notes: Good Sunday lunch. Clean and light.

recipes.name: Spring Pasta Primavera with Prosciutto, Peas & Arugula
recipes.spice_level: Low (Austin: add red pepper flakes freely)
recipes.equipment: Large pot, large skillet
instructions: Boil well-salted water. Cook pasta al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water before draining.
Heat olive oil in large skillet over medium. Add shallots; cook 3 min.
Add garlic; cook 1 min. Add cherry tomatoes; cook 4 min until bursting.
Add peas; cook 2 min. Tear in prosciutto; warm through 1 min.
Add drained pasta. Toss with pasta water to loosen. Add arugula; toss until just wilted.
Off heat: add parmesan, lemon juice, lemon zest, pepper flakes. Toss vigorously.
Taste, season, and plate immediately.
recipes.batch_note: Make fresh Monday evening. Arugula wilts fast — don't batch this one.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: use 1/4 less pasta, extra cherry tomatoes, extra arugula.
recipes.seasonal_note: This dish IS spring in a bowl. Don't fully cook the arugula — you want it wilted but still bright green and peppery.

ratings.notes: Solid Monday dinner. Spring peas were the right call.

recipes.name: Thai Basil Chicken Stir-Fry with Jasmine Rice & Fried Egg
recipes.equipment: Wok or large skillet, separate small pan for eggs

ingredients.name: Spring onions, whites and greens separated

instructions: Whisk together all sauce ingredients. Set aside.
Heat wok or large skillet over HIGH heat until smoking. Add 1 tbsp oil.
Add chicken — cook 4-5 min, stirring, until cooked through with charred edges.
Add garlic, ginger, and white spring onion parts. Cook 60 seconds.
Add chiles (Austin) or jalapeno (Cameron). Toss.
Pour sauce over chicken. Toss to coat. Cook 1-2 min until reduced slightly.
Off heat: fold in basil — it wilts immediately. Add green spring onion tops.
In separate pan: fry 1 egg per person in a little oil — runny yolk.
Serve chicken over rice. Top with fried egg. Austin: extra chiles on side.
recipes.batch_note: Make fresh Tuesday. Fast weeknight cook. The fried egg on top is mandatory — runny yolk breaks into the rice and creates the sauce.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: use 1 jalapeño instead of bird's eye chiles. Keep the sauce bold. Extra oyster sauce for richness.
recipes.seasonal_note: Thai basil has an anise-clove note Italian basil doesn't. Find it at any Asian grocery or Whole Foods.

ratings.notes: Thai basil was a hit. Would repeat.

recipes.name: Loaded Chicken Fajita Bowls with Spring Onion Crema
recipes.equipment: Cast iron or tabletop griddle, blender for crema

ingredients.name: Boneless chicken thighs, sliced into strips

instructions: Blend crema: yogurt, spring onions, lime juice, garlic, salt — blitz until smooth and bright green. Refrigerate.
Toss chicken strips with cumin, chili powder, paprika, garlic powder, salt, 1 tbsp oil.
Heat cast iron over HIGH. Cook chicken 4-5 min per side until charred and cooked through. Remove.
Same pan: cook peppers and red onion 6-8 min with some char. Add jalapeno (Austin) last 2 min.
Squeeze lime over peppers. Toss.
Build bowls: rice + black beans, then fajita chicken and peppers on top.
Drizzle spring onion crema generously. Cameron: add sliced avocado. Lime over everything.
recipes.batch_note: Make fresh Wednesday. Spring onion crema takes 3 min in a blender and is the star of the dish.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: serve as bowl over rice. Skip jalapeno from her portion. Add sliced avocado on top.
recipes.seasonal_note: Spring onions give the crema a fresh mild brightness that beats any store-bought version.

ratings.notes: Felt a bit plain — needs more char and heat next time.

recipes.name: Miso Glazed Salmon with Roasted Asparagus & Sesame Rice
recipes.equipment: Sheet pan, oven, foil

ingredients.name: Mirin or 1 tbsp honey + 1 tbsp rice vinegar

instructions: Whisk glaze. Coat salmon fillets fully. Marinate 30 min to 8 hrs in fridge.
Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a sheet pan with foil.
Toss asparagus with olive oil, salt, pepper. Spread on one half of pan.
Place salmon skin-side-down on other half. Roast 10-12 min.
Switch to BROIL. Broil 2-3 min until glaze caramelizes. Watch closely — miso burns fast.
Warm rice and toss with sesame oil and soy sauce.
Plate: sesame rice, asparagus alongside, salmon on top. Garnish with spring onions, sesame seeds, lemon wedge.
recipes.batch_note: Marinate salmon Thursday morning or night before. Sheet pan dinner — asparagus roasts while salmon glazes.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: same glaze, reduce broil by 1 min. She prefers slightly less char.
recipes.seasonal_note: Asparagus and miso salmon is a classic spring pairing. Pittsburgh asparagus is peak right now.

ratings.notes: Really good — requested repeat for upcoming weeks.

recipes.name: Turkey Meatballs & Spaghetti Pomodoro
recipes.equipment: Large oven-safe skillet, large pot for pasta
instructions: Mix turkey, breadcrumbs, parmesan, garlic, basil, egg, Italian seasoning, salt, pepper. Don't overmix.
Roll into golf-ball sized meatballs (~14-16 total).
Heat large oven-safe skillet over medium-high with 1 tbsp olive oil. Brown meatballs all sides, 2-3 min per side.
Pour pomodoro sauce over meatballs. Simmer covered 10-12 min until 165°F internal.
Cook spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve 1/4 cup pasta water. Drain.
Toss spaghetti with a ladle of the meatball sauce to coat.
Plate spaghetti, top with meatballs and sauce. Finish with parmesan, fresh basil, and pepper flakes for Austin.
recipes.batch_note: Make meatballs fresh Friday. Doubles well — make 20, freeze 10 for next week.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: 4 oz spaghetti instead of 5 oz. Extra sauce and extra parmesan on top.
recipes.seasonal_note: Fresh basil in the meatball mix is the spring upgrade. It lifts this from a cold-weather dish into early May territory.

recipes.name: Greek Lamb Keftedes with Arugula Salad & Herbed Tzatziki
recipes.equipment: Cast iron skillet, mixing bowl
instructions: Make tzatziki: mix all ingredients, season well. Refrigerate at least 30 min — overnight is better.
Combine ground lamb with garlic, mint, dill, cumin, oregano, pepper flakes, salt, pepper. Mix gently.
Form into small oval patties about 2 inches long (8-10 total).
Heat cast iron over medium-high with 1 tbsp olive oil. Cook keftedes 3-4 min per side until browned at 160°F.
While keftedes cook, toss arugula, tomatoes, red onion with olive oil, lemon, salt, pepper.
Plate: arugula base, keftedes alongside, tzatziki spooned over. Crumble feta over salad.
Cameron: add sliced avocado to salad, extra feta. Offer warm pita if desired.
recipes.batch_note: Make tzatziki Friday evening — it gets better overnight. Keftedes cook fast Saturday fresh.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 sliced avocado and extra feta on the arugula. Consider a warm pita on the side.
recipes.seasonal_note: Fresh mint in keftedes is non-negotiable for spring. It brightens the lamb completely.

ratings.notes: Requested repeat. Lamb + feta combo landed perfectly.

recipes.name: Smoker Baby Back Ribs with New Potatoes & Arugula Slaw
recipes.prep: 20 min (+ overnight dry rub Sat eve)
recipes.spice_level: High Austin (bold rub) | Medium Cameron (half cayenne)
recipes.equipment: Smoker + apple/cherry wood, sheet pan (potatoes), large bowl (slaw)

ingredients.name: Baby back ribs, 2 full racks ~5-6 lbs

instructions: SAT NIGHT: Remove membrane from back of ribs. Apply dry rub all over — press it in. Wrap in plastic. Refrigerate overnight.
SUN MORNING: Pull ribs 30 min before smoking. Fire smoker to 225°F. Add apple or cherry wood.
PHASE 1 (3 hrs): Ribs meat-side up on grate, unwrapped. Building bark and smoke ring.
PHASE 2 (2 hrs): Wrap each rack in foil with 1 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp brown sugar inside. Return to smoker.
PHASE 3 (1 hr): Unwrap ribs. Brush generously with BBQ sauce. Smoke uncovered. Target: 195-203°F internal.
REST: Tent loosely with foil 15 min before slicing between bones.
POTATOES (35 min before ribs done): Toss with olive oil, thyme, salt, pepper. Roast at 425°F for 25 min.
SLAW: Toss arugula, sliced radishes, spring onions with lemon-Dijon dressing just before serving.
Plate: ribs, potatoes, slaw. Cold beer optional but strongly encouraged.
recipes.batch_note: Apply dry rub SATURDAY NIGHT. Start smoker Sunday morning early. This is the project dinner.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: 3-4 ribs, larger potato serving. Arugula slaw is no-cabbage — toss lightly so it stays fresh.
recipes.seasonal_note: Baby back ribs smoked over apple wood in late April is one of the great Pittsburgh spring rituals.

ratings.notes: Excellent on the smoker. Best thing we made that week.

recipes.name: Strawberry Rhubarb Protein Yogurt Bowl
recipes.equipment: 4 meal prep containers, small saucepan

ingredients.name: RHUBARB COMPOTE (Sunday, 1 batch covers the week)

instructions: COMPOTE (Sunday): Combine rhubarb, honey, and water in small saucepan over medium heat.
Cook 5-6 min, stirring occasionally, until rhubarb breaks down into a jammy consistency.
Cool completely. Store in a jar — it keeps 7 days refrigerated.
BOWLS (Sunday batch): Whisk yogurt + protein powder in each container until completely smooth. Seal.
Store compote jar and bag of strawberries in fridge alongside containers.
Morning-of: stir compote into yogurt, top with sliced strawberries and granola.
Austin: drizzle almond butter + honey on top.
recipes.batch_note: Make rhubarb compote Sunday — it takes 6 min and changes the whole bowl. Portion yogurt + protein into 4 containers. Add compote, berries, granola morning-of.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: 3/4 cup yogurt, skip almond butter. Add side of avocado if she wants healthy fat.
recipes.seasonal_note: Rhubarb is peak in Pittsburgh right now — tart, bright, and completely spring. Worth the extra 6 minutes.

recipes.name: Spring Asparagus & Turkey Egg Bites
recipes.equipment: 12-cup muffin tin, large mixing bowl, whisk
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin thoroughly.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs and egg whites until fully combined and slightly frothy.
Fold in turkey sausage, asparagus tips, spring onions, feta, garlic powder, pepper flakes, salt, pepper.
Pour evenly into muffin cups — fill each about 3/4 full.
Bake 18-20 min until puffed and set in the center.
Cool in tin 5 min, then transfer to wire rack. Cool FULLY before storing.
Store airtight in fridge. Reheat before eating.
recipes.batch_note: Bake all 12 Sunday. Reheat Breville 325°F 8 min or microwave 60 sec. Last 5 days.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: 3 bites. Add 1/4 sliced avocado on the side morning-of.
recipes.seasonal_note: The asparagus tips caramelize at the top of each bite — that's the tell that you used fresh seasonal asparagus.

recipes.name: Korean BBQ Chicken Bowl with Gochujang & Pickled Radish
recipes.prep: 15 min (assembly — chicken + pickled radish from batch)
recipes.equipment: 2 meal prep containers per person, small jar for sauce

macro_strings.cameron: 510 cal | 36g P | 12g F | 55g C  (+60 cal, 3g F for 1/4 avocado)

instructions: PICKLED RADISH: toss sliced radishes with rice vinegar, sugar, salt. Rest 30 min minimum. Gets better overnight.
KOREAN BBQ SAUCE: whisk all sauce ingredients until smooth. Store in small jar.
Build bowl: rice base, chicken, edamame, spinach, spring onions.
Top with pickled radish and sesame seeds.
Keep sauce separate. Drizzle and toss day-of.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado, half the sauce amount.
recipes.batch_note: Assemble 2 containers per person Sunday. Pickled radish and sauce both made Sunday — they improve overnight.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado fresh daily. Lighter on the sauce.
recipes.seasonal_note: Pickled radishes are a spring staple — crisp, pink, and aggressively bright against the rich gochujang.

recipes.name: Thai Peanut Chicken Soba Noodle Bowl
recipes.equipment: Large pot, 2 meal prep containers per person, sauce jar

macro_strings.cameron: 515 cal | 36g P | 15g F | 52g C  (+60 cal for 1/4 avocado)

ingredients.name: Batch chicken thighs, sliced or shredded

instructions: Cook soba noodles per package (typically 4-5 min boiling water). Drain, rinse under cold water.
Toss noodles with 1 tsp sesame oil to prevent clumping. Set aside.
SAUCE: whisk all sauce ingredients. Add warm water 1 tbsp at a time until pourable.
Assemble containers: noodles, chicken, edamame, spinach, spring onions.
Top with sesame seeds. Keep sauce in a small jar.
Day-of: pour sauce over bowl, toss well. Squeeze lime over top.
Cameron: half sauce, add 1/4 avocado, extra lime.
recipes.batch_note: Cook soba noodles Sunday, rinse cold, toss with sesame oil so they don't clump. Lasts 4 days.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: lighter on the Sriracha. Add 1/4 avocado day-of. Extra lime squeeze.
recipes.seasonal_note: Soba noodles + peanut + spring onions + lime is a texture and flavor shift from rice bowls — same macro efficiency, completely different eating experience.

recipes.name: Spring Arugula & Prosciutto Salad with Soft Boiled Egg
recipes.equipment: Small pot for eggs, ice bowl, salad bowl

macro_strings.cameron: 510 cal | 35g P | 18g F | 36g C  (+60 cal for 1/4 avocado)

instructions: SOFT BOILED EGGS: Bring water to full boil. Lower eggs in gently. Cook 7 min for jammy yolk. Transfer immediately to ice bath 5 min. Store unpeeled in fridge.
LEMON VINAIGRETTE: whisk all ingredients. Adjust lemon and salt. Store in small jar.
Assemble base: arugula, cherry tomatoes, white beans, feta.
Peel eggs just before eating — halve and place on top. Tear prosciutto over the salad.
Drizzle vinaigrette and toss gently. Eat immediately.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado sliced, extra feta, extra lemon squeeze.
recipes.batch_note: Hard-boil or soft-boil eggs in advance (store unpeeled, 5 days). Pack prosciutto separately so it doesn't wilt the arugula.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado, extra feta, extra lemon. Prosciutto goes salty-creamy with the avocado.
recipes.seasonal_note: This is a proper spring lunch — peppery arugula, jammy eggs, salty prosciutto, creamy white beans.

recipes.name: Smoked Chicken & Butter Lettuce Wraps with Pickled Ginger
recipes.serving_note: 1 per person — Sunday lunch (from beer can chicken leftovers)
recipes.equipment: None — just assembly

macro_strings.cameron: 505 cal | 36g P | 14g F | 48g C  (+60 cal for 1/4 avocado)

instructions: PICKLED GINGER (optional, Sat): thinly slice fresh ginger. Toss with rice vinegar, sugar, salt. Rest 30 min. Fridge 5 days.
SAUCE: whisk soy, sesame oil, rice vinegar, ginger, honey, garlic. Taste and adjust.
Shred smoked chicken from the bird — mix light and dark meat for best flavor.
Lay butter lettuce leaves flat. Add a spoonful of rice to each.
Top with shredded chicken, spring onions, sesame seeds, and pickled ginger.
Spoon sauce over wraps or serve alongside for dipping.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado into the wraps.
recipes.batch_note: Carve smoked chicken while still warm — pull 1/4 bird per person for lunch. Assemble immediately after carving.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado sliced into the wraps.
recipes.seasonal_note: The contrast between cold crisp butter lettuce and warm smoky chicken is the payoff here.

recipes.name: Lemon Chicken Piccata with Asparagus & Orzo
recipes.equipment: Large skillet, pot for orzo, baking sheet for asparagus

ingredients.name: Dry white wine or chicken broth (pantry)

instructions: Cook orzo in well-salted boiling water per package. Drain. Toss with 1 tsp olive oil. Set aside.
Pound chicken thighs to even 1/2-inch thickness. Season with salt and pepper. Dust both sides lightly with flour.
Heat 1.5 tbsp olive oil in large skillet over medium-high. Cook chicken 3-4 min per side until golden. Remove to plate.
Same pan, medium heat: sauté shallots 2 min. Add garlic 1 min.
Add wine or broth to deglaze — scrape up all the brown bits. Add lemon juice, lemon slices, capers. Simmer 2-3 min.
Off heat: swirl in butter. It should make a glossy sauce. Return chicken to pan, spoon sauce over. Finish with lemon zest.
ASPARAGUS: toss with olive oil, salt, pepper. Roast at 425°F or grill in a pan 6-8 min.
Plate: orzo, asparagus alongside, chicken with sauce poured over. Parmesan + parsley on top.
recipes.batch_note: Make fresh Monday evening. The caper-lemon pan sauce comes together in 5 min once the chicken is done.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: same dish, slightly smaller chicken portion. More orzo if she wants it.
recipes.seasonal_note: Peak asparagus + capers + lemon is peak May cooking. The orzo soaks up the piccata sauce like pasta should.

recipes.name: Za'atar Shrimp with Spring Pea Couscous & Arugula
recipes.equipment: Large skillet, large bowl for couscous
instructions: COUSCOUS: combine dry couscous in bowl with 1 tbsp olive oil, pinch salt. Pour boiling water/broth over (1:1 ratio). Cover tightly 5 min. Fluff with fork.
Fold in thawed peas, mint, lemon juice, lemon zest. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
ZA'ATAR SHRIMP: toss shrimp with za'atar, salt, pepper, and 1/2 tbsp olive oil.
Heat remaining olive oil in large skillet over medium-high. Add garlic 30 sec.
Add shrimp in single layer. Cook 2 min per side until pink and curled.
ARUGULA: toss with a drizzle of olive oil, lemon juice, salt.
Plate: pea couscous base, arugula alongside, shrimp on top. Crumble feta over everything.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado sliced on the arugula. Extra feta.
recipes.batch_note: Make fresh Tuesday. Shrimp cook in under 4 min — don't overcook.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado on top of the arugula.
recipes.seasonal_note: Za'atar on shrimp is the upgrade move — nutty, herby, slightly tangy from sumac in the blend.

recipes.name: Coconut Green Curry Chicken with Jasmine Rice
recipes.spice_level: High Austin (extra jalapeño) | Medium Cameron (1 tbsp paste, no jalapeño)
recipes.equipment: Large skillet or wok

macro_strings.cameron: 590 cal | 37g P | 18g F | 70g C  (extra sauce for Cameron)

instructions: Heat oil in large skillet or wok over medium-high. Add ginger, garlic, spring onion whites — cook 1 min.
Add curry paste (Austin: 2 tbsp | Cameron: 1 tbsp). Stir-fry 1 min until fragrant.
Add chicken. Cook 5-6 min until no longer pink, stirring to coat in curry paste.
Pour in coconut milk. Stir to combine. Add fish sauce, honey, and jalapeño (Austin).
Add sliced bell peppers. Simmer 8-10 min until peppers are tender and sauce thickens slightly.
Add lime juice. Taste and adjust — more fish sauce for salt, more lime for brightness.
Off heat: fold in spinach or Thai basil — it wilts immediately.
Serve over jasmine rice. Top with cilantro and spring onion greens.
recipes.batch_note: Make fresh Wednesday. The curry paste + coconut milk + fish sauce base comes together in under 10 min.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: 1 tbsp curry paste, no jalapeño. More coconut milk for a creamier, milder sauce. She will want extra rice for the sauce.
recipes.seasonal_note: Green curry screams spring — it's lighter and brighter than red.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Salmon Bowls with Pickled Cucumber & Sesame Rice
recipes.equipment: Sheet pan, oven/broiler, foil
instructions: GLAZE: Whisk soy, honey, rice vinegar, ginger, garlic, sesame oil in a small bowl.
Pour half the glaze over salmon. Marinate 20 min to overnight. Reserve remaining glaze.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a sheet pan with foil.
Place salmon skin-side-down. Roast 10-12 min until mostly opaque.
Switch to BROIL. Brush with remaining glaze. Broil 2-3 min until caramelized. Watch closely — honey burns fast.
SESAME RICE: warm batch rice in a pan with sesame oil and soy sauce — toss to coat.
EDAMAME: thaw in warm water or microwave 2 min.
Plate: sesame rice, edamame, pickled cucumber, salmon on top.
recipes.batch_note: Marinate salmon Thursday morning or night before. Pickled cucumber made Sunday.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: same dish. The teriyaki glaze is sweet-savory and not spicy — zero adjustments needed.
recipes.seasonal_note: Teriyaki is a different direction from miso — sweeter, less funky, brighter.

recipes.name: Spicy Ground Turkey Street Tacos with Spring Onion Pico
recipes.spice_level: High Austin | Medium Cameron (reduce cayenne + skip jalapeño)
recipes.equipment: Large skillet, gas burner or cast iron for tortillas
instructions: PICO: combine spring onions, tomatoes, jalapeño, cilantro, lime juice, salt. Toss and let sit 10 min.
Heat olive oil in large skillet over medium-high. Add ground turkey — break apart with spoon. Cook 6-8 min until cooked through with some caramelization.
Add all taco seasonings. Toss to coat. Add 2 tbsp water and stir. Cook 1-2 min.
TORTILLAS: char corn tortillas directly over a gas flame 30-45 sec per side until blistered. Or dry cast iron, 1 min per side.
Warm black beans in a small pot or microwave.
BUILD TACOS: tortilla, spoonful of black beans, turkey, generous pico on top.
Austin: extra jalapeño, hot sauce, lime. Cameron: sliced avocado, lighter on seasoning.
recipes.batch_note: Make fresh Friday. Spring onion pico is the difference-maker — don't sub regular white onion.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: cut cayenne in half, skip extra jalapeño. Add sliced avocado.
recipes.seasonal_note: Spring onions in the pico instead of white onion is the spring upgrade — less aggressive, greener, and far more interesting.

recipes.name: Chicken Souvlaki Skewers with Herbed Tzatziki & Spring Salad
recipes.spice_level: Medium Austin | Low Cameron (small pinch pepper flakes)
recipes.equipment: Skewers (metal or soaked wood), cast iron or grill, small mixing bowl for tzatziki
instructions: TZATZIKI (Friday): Mix yogurt, grated squeezed cucumber, garlic, dill, mint, lemon, salt. Refrigerate overnight.
MARINADE: Whisk olive oil, lemon, garlic, oregano, thyme, pepper flakes. Add chicken cubes. Marinate 30 min to 2 hrs.
Thread chicken onto skewers (2-3 skewers per person, 3-4 pieces each).
GRILL OR CAST IRON: high heat, oiled surface. Cook skewers 3-4 min per side, turning twice, until charred at 165°F internal.
SALAD: toss arugula, tomatoes, red onion with lemon vinaigrette. Top with feta.
WARM PITA: wrap in foil, Breville 5 min at 350°F or dry skillet 1 min per side.
Plate: skewers alongside salad, generous tzatziki on the side.
Cameron: add 1/4 avocado to salad.
recipes.batch_note: Marinate chicken Saturday morning. Make tzatziki Friday night — overnight is better.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado to salad and an extra warm pita if she wants more substance.
recipes.seasonal_note: Fresh dill and mint in the tzatziki is non-negotiable right now — they're both peak spring herbs.

recipes.name: Beer Can Smoked Whole Chicken with New Potatoes & Grilled Asparagus
recipes.prep: 20 min (+ overnight dry rub Sat eve)
recipes.spice_level: Medium-High Austin (bold rub) | Medium Cameron (lighter cayenne)
recipes.serving_note: 2–4 (Sunday dinner + leftover meat for Sunday lunch wraps)
recipes.equipment: Smoker + apple/cherry wood, sheet pan (potatoes + asparagus), kitchen thermometer

ingredients.name: 1 can lager beer
ingredients.qty: 12 oz — half for drinking, half for the cavity

ingredients.name: Cayenne (pantry)
ingredients.qty: 1 tsp Austin side / 1/2 tsp Cameron side

instructions: SAT NIGHT: Pat chicken dry inside and out. Remove giblets. Loosen skin over breast with fingers.
Apply dry rub all over — under skin on breast, inside cavity, all over exterior. Press it in.
Wrap loosely in plastic wrap. Refrigerate overnight. Chill a beer can.
SUN MORNING: Pull chicken 30 min before smoking. Open beer can, pour out half.
Lower chicken cavity onto beer can — it stands upright. Place upright on smoker grate.
Smoke at 275°F with apple or cherry wood. 3.5–4 hrs total until 165°F in the breast.
REST: Remove from smoker. Let rest 15 min before carving.
CARVE: Remove breast carefully. Legs and thighs separate. Reserve 1/4 bird for Sunday lunch wraps.
POTATOES: toss with olive oil, thyme, salt, pepper. Roast at 425°F for 25-30 min.
ASPARAGUS: toss with olive oil, lemon, salt. Broil or grill 6-8 min until charred tips.
Plate: carved chicken, roasted potatoes, grilled asparagus.
recipes.batch_note: Apply dry rub Saturday night. Start smoker by 8-9am Sunday. Reserve 1/4 of the bird carved warm for Sunday lunch lettuce wraps.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: half cayenne in the dry rub on her half of the bird. She gets white meat (breast) at dinner.
recipes.seasonal_note: Beer can smoked chicken in May with asparagus and new potatoes is spring BBQ done right — the beer steams the cavity from inside while smoke works the outside.

recipes.name: Strawberry Mango Protein Smoothie Bowl
recipes.equipment: High-powered blender, 4 freezer-safe meal prep containers
instructions: SATURDAY BATCH: Blend each serving base separately (or in 2 batches of 2). Combine frozen mango + frozen strawberries + Greek yogurt + protein powder + almond milk. Blend on high until completely smooth and very thick — much thicker than a drinkable smoothie. It should hold a spoon upright.
Pour into individual meal prep containers. Cover tightly and freeze overnight.
MORNING-OF: Pull container from freezer 15–20 minutes before eating. It should be the consistency of soft-serve or thick sorbet.
Top Austin's bowl with granola + fresh strawberry slices + 1 tbsp almond butter.
Top Cameron's bowl with granola + fresh strawberry slices + coconut flakes.
Eat immediately — do not refreeze once thawed.
recipes.batch_note: Blend 4 bases Saturday night, freeze in containers. Pull each one out 15-20 min before eating. Add toppings fresh morning-of.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron skips almond butter — uses coconut flakes instead. Lighter on the mango if preferred.
recipes.seasonal_note: Strawberries are at peak in late May Pittsburgh. Use fresh for toppings, frozen for the base blend.

recipes.name: Egg White & Veggie Frittata Cups with Turkey & Snap Peas
recipes.equipment: 12-cup muffin tin, large mixing bowl, non-stick spray

ingredients.name: Spring onions, thinly sliced (whites + light green)
AUSTIN: 4 cups per serving + optional hot sauce
CAMERON: 3 cups per serving + optional avocado side (1/4 avocado)

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Spray a 12-cup muffin tin generously with non-stick spray — get the sides well coated.
In a large bowl, whisk together egg whites and whole eggs until smooth and slightly foamy.
Add cooked turkey sausage crumbles, chopped snap peas, sliced spring onions, feta, garlic powder, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Ladle mixture evenly into prepared muffin cups, filling each about 3/4 full. The mixture will puff up during baking.
Bake 20–22 minutes until tops are puffed, golden, and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. They should spring back when gently pressed.
Cool in tin for 5 minutes, then run a butter knife around each cup and pop out. Cool completely on a rack before storing.
Store airtight in fridge up to 5 days. Reheat in microwave 45–60 seconds or in air fryer at 350°F for 3–4 min.
Austin: 4 cups per serving. Cameron: 3 cups per serving, with optional fresh avocado slices on the side.
recipes.batch_note: Bake all 12 cups Sunday. Cool fully before storing airtight. Reheat 45 sec in microwave or 3 min in air fryer.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: 3 cups per serving. Add 1/4 avocado on the side fresh each morning.
recipes.seasonal_note: Snap peas instead of asparagus this week — late spring transition. Still bright and green.

recipes.name: Caprese Chicken Orzo Bowl with Fresh Mozzarella, Cherry Tomatoes & Basil
recipes.equipment: Large pot for orzo, meal prep containers

ingredients.name: Dry orzo pasta, cooked al dente
Caprese drizzle (olive oil + balsamic glaze + garlic)
Dry orzo pasta, cooked al dente

instructions: SUNDAY ORZO BATCH: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil. Cook orzo until al dente per package (about 8 min). Drain and immediately rinse with cold water. Toss with a tiny drizzle of olive oil to prevent sticking.
MAKE CAPRESE DRIZZLE: Whisk 3 tbsp olive oil + 1.5 tbsp balsamic glaze + 1/2 tsp garlic powder + salt + pepper. Store in a small jar.
ASSEMBLE CONTAINERS: Divide cold orzo into containers. Top with sliced batch chicken, mozzarella, cherry tomatoes, and sun-dried tomatoes.
Drizzle caprese dressing over everything. Season with salt and pepper.
Store basil separately in a small bag — add torn leaves day-of so they don't wilt. Cameron adds 1/4 avocado sliced on day-of as well.
Eat cold or at room temp. Will keep refrigerated 3–4 days.
recipes.batch_note: Cook orzo Sunday. Assemble containers fully except basil and Cameron's avocado. Both added day-of.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 sliced avocado and extra basil day-of. Caprese drizzle holds everything together.
recipes.seasonal_note: Cherry tomatoes and fresh mozzarella are the spring-to-summer bridge here.

recipes.name: Spicy Thai Chicken Cucumber Noodle Salad with Soba & Sesame Lime Dressing
recipes.cook: 0 min (chicken from batch, soba from batch)
recipes.equipment: Meal prep containers, small jar for dressing

ingredients.name: Batch-roasted sesame-ginger chicken thighs, sliced thin
Persian cucumbers, sliced into thin rounds
Batch-roasted sesame-ginger chicken thighs, sliced thin
Mild chili oil or light Sriracha

instructions: SUNDAY DRESSING BATCH: Whisk all dressing ingredients together. Taste — adjust lime and soy to balance. Store in a small jar in fridge up to 1 week.
ASSEMBLE CONTAINERS (Sunday): Divide cold soba noodles into containers. Top with sliced sesame-ginger batch chicken.
Add cucumber rounds, spring onions, shredded carrots, and snap peas. Drizzle with sesame-lime dressing.
Store cilantro separately in a small bag — add day-of. Cameron's avocado is always sliced fresh and added day-of.
Sprinkle sesame seeds over top. Austin adds Sriracha or chili oil when eating. Cameron uses a lighter hand on heat.
Eat cold — this salad is best chilled. Will keep 3–4 days refrigerated (noodles may absorb dressing; re-toss before eating).
recipes.batch_note: Make sesame-lime dressing Sunday. Assemble noodle bowls with all components except cilantro and Cameron's avocado. Both added fresh day-of.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: lighter chili, add 1/4 avocado fresh. The avocado cools the heat perfectly.
recipes.seasonal_note: Persian cucumbers and snap peas are late spring heroes. Crunchy, fresh, bright — exactly what this salad needs.

recipes.name: Watermelon Arugula Grilled Chicken Salad with Feta, Mint & Red Wine Vinaigrette
recipes.prep: 10 min (slice chicken + watermelon Sunday; dress day-of)
recipes.equipment: Meal prep containers, jar for dressing
instructions: SUNDAY PREP: Make vinaigrette by shaking all dressing ingredients in a small jar. Taste and adjust acidity.
Cube watermelon. Store in a separate container — do NOT store with arugula or it will wilt everything.
Slice batch chicken thighs and store in containers.
Store arugula, watermelon, and chicken all SEPARATELY until day-of. Assemble just before eating for best texture.
DAY-OF ASSEMBLY: Toss arugula with a drizzle of vinaigrette. Top with chicken, watermelon cubes, feta, red onion, and torn mint. Drizzle remaining dressing over top.
Cameron adds 1/4 sliced avocado on top. Finish with cracked pepper.
IMPORTANT: Do not dress this salad in advance — watermelon releases liquid and arugula wilts fast. Assemble and eat within 5 minutes of dressing.
recipes.batch_note: Prep and store all components separately Sunday. DO NOT dress in advance — assemble day-of only. Watermelon releases liquid fast.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado on top, extra feta. The avocado + watermelon + feta combo is outstanding.
recipes.seasonal_note: Watermelon is just hitting peak in late May. This is a seasonal window meal — grab a good one.

recipes.name: Lemon Ricotta Spring Pasta with Snap Peas, Prosciutto & Parmesan
recipes.serving_note: Serves 2 — Austin + Cameron with different portions
recipes.equipment: Large pot, large skillet or Le Creuset
instructions: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a rolling boil. Cook pasta until al dente per package. IMPORTANT: reserve 1/2 cup pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add shallots and cook 2 min until softened. Add garlic and cook 1 min more.
Add prosciutto pieces and let them crisp up slightly, 2–3 min, stirring occasionally. Remove pan from heat.
Add snap peas to pasta water for the last 90 seconds of cooking — they should still have snap. Drain pasta and peas together.

Return skillet to medium-low heat. Add drained pasta + snap peas. Add ricotta, lemon zest, lemon juice, and a splash of pasta water. Toss everything together, adding more pasta water as needed to create a creamy, silky sauce — not watery.
Remove from heat. Stir in arugula until just wilted, about 30 seconds. Season aggressively with salt and pepper.
Plate Austin's portion first with more red pepper flakes. Plate Cameron's with a pinch of flakes and lighter lemon.
Finish both plates with freshly grated parmesan and torn basil. Eat immediately.
recipes.batch_note: Not a batch meal — cook to order Monday night. 30 min start to finish.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: lighter on red pepper flakes, extra lemon zest. The ricotta sauce is naturally creamy and satisfying.
recipes.seasonal_note: Snap peas and prosciutto make this feel like late-spring Italy. The arugula wilted in at the end adds a peppery kick.

recipes.name: Greek Chicken Gyro Plates with Tzatziki, Warm Pita & Watercress Salad
recipes.cook: 0 min (chicken from batch, tzatziki from batch)
recipes.equipment: Skillet or air fryer for pita warming

ingredients.name: Batch-roasted Italian chicken thighs, sliced gyro-style

instructions: Warm pitas in a dry skillet over medium-high for 30–45 seconds per side until puffed and slightly charred, or in air fryer at 400°F for 2 min. Keep warm wrapped in a clean towel.
Slice batch-roasted Italian chicken thighs thin on the diagonal — gyro style. If desired, quickly reheat in a hot skillet with a drizzle of olive oil for 2–3 min to get some char on the edges.
Toss watercress with olive oil, lemon juice, fresh dill, and a pinch of salt.
BUILD THE PLATES: Lay warm pita at the base. Pile on sliced chicken. Spoon tzatziki generously over chicken. Add cherry tomatoes, sliced red onion, spring onions, and feta.
Place the watercress salad alongside on the plate. Finish with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of dried oregano.
Cameron gets 1/4 avocado sliced on her watercress salad. Serve immediately with extra lemon on the side.
recipes.batch_note: Tzatziki made Sunday. Chicken from batch. Assembly is 15 min Tuesday night — warm pita, slice chicken, build plates.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado fanned on the watercress salad. Extra tzatziki on the side.
recipes.seasonal_note: Watercress is at its peppery best right now. It's the upgrade over plain lettuce in this gyro plate.

recipes.name: Thai Drunken Noodles with Ground Turkey, Thai Basil & Spring Onions
recipes.equipment: Large wok or skillet, rice noodle soak bowl

ingredients.name: Fresh Thai basil leaves (NOT Italian basil)
Bird's eye chilies OR red pepper flakes
Dark soy sauce or extra soy

instructions: SOAK NOODLES: Place dry wide rice noodles in a large bowl. Pour hot (not boiling) water over them. Soak 20–25 min until pliable but not fully soft — they'll finish in the wok. Drain and toss with a drop of oil.
MIX SAUCE: In a small bowl, combine oyster sauce + soy sauce + fish sauce + dark soy + sugar. Stir and set aside.
Heat wok or large skillet over HIGH heat until smoking. Add neutral oil. Add garlic, ginger, and chilies (Austin full amount; Cameron half) — stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add ground turkey. Break up and cook 4–5 min until no pink remains and edges start to caramelize.
Add bell peppers and spring onions — stir-fry 2 min. Push everything to the side. Crack eggs into the wok and scramble them in the empty space for 60 seconds, then fold into the turkey.
Add soaked noodles and pour sauce over everything. Toss vigorously with tongs for 2–3 min until noodles are fully cooked, coated in sauce, and getting some color.
Remove from heat. Add Thai basil leaves and toss — they'll wilt from residual heat. Drizzle sesame oil over top.
Plate Austin's portion with extra chili. Plate Cameron's with extra Thai basil and a lighter hand on heat. Serve with lime wedges to squeeze over top.
recipes.batch_note: Cook to order Wednesday night. Soak noodles 20 min before starting. 25 min total.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: half the bird's eye chili, extra Thai basil. Serve with lime wedges and extra sauce on the side.
recipes.seasonal_note: Thai basil is key — do not sub Italian basil. The anise note makes the dish.

recipes.name: Miso Butter Chicken Thighs with Sesame Soba Noodles & Snap Peas
recipes.equipment: Large skillet, small saucepan for sauce

ingredients.name: Batch-roasted sesame-ginger chicken thighs
ingredients.qty: 6 oz Austin / 5 oz Cameron — reheat in skillet

ingredients.name: Fresh snap peas, trimmed
ingredients.qty: 1 cup total — blanch or air fry

ingredients.name: MISO BUTTER SAUCE (batch — see Sunday sauces)

instructions: MISO BUTTER SAUCE (if not made Sunday): In a small saucepan over low heat, melt butter. Whisk in miso, soy, mirin, sesame oil, and ginger until smooth. Do not boil — keep low heat. Remove and set aside.

BLANCH SNAP PEAS: Boil 1 cup snap peas for 60–90 seconds in salted water. Drain and immediately shock in cold water. They should be bright green and still crunchy. OR air fry at 400°F for 4 min with a drizzle of sesame oil and pinch of salt.
REHEAT SOBA: Toss cold soba noodles in a skillet with 1 tbsp soy sauce + 1 tsp sesame oil over medium heat, 2–3 min until warmed through. Or microwave 60 seconds.
REHEAT CHICKEN: Heat batch-roasted sesame-ginger chicken in a skillet over medium-high with a tiny drizzle of sesame oil. 2–3 min per side to warm through and re-crisp the edges.
PLATE: Divide soba into bowls. Drizzle warm miso butter sauce over noodles and toss to coat. Top with sliced chicken thighs.
Arrange snap peas alongside. Garnish with spring onions, sesame seeds, and dill/cilantro.
Serve immediately. Austin can add a drizzle of chili oil or Sriracha for heat.
recipes.batch_note: Miso butter sauce made Sunday. Soba from batch. Assembly is 20 min Thursday — reheat components and plate.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: same dish, slightly smaller chicken portion. Add a drizzle of sesame oil and extra dill garnish.
recipes.seasonal_note: Snap peas charred in the air fryer are the seasonal star — bright green, crisp, slightly sweet.

recipes.name: Chipotle Chicken Burrito Bowls with Cilantro Lime Rice & Spring Pico
recipes.equipment: Skillet, rice cooker or pot for cilantro lime rice

ingredients.name: Batch-roasted Italian chicken thighs, shredded + tossed in chipotle sauce
Chipotle peppers in adobo, minced
ingredients.qty: 1.5 tbsp Austin / 1 tsp Cameron — BIG difference

instructions: MAKE CILANTRO LIME RICE: Reheat batch jasmine rice in a skillet or microwave. Toss warm rice with 1 tbsp lime juice + lime zest + 2 tbsp chopped cilantro + pinch of salt. Taste and adjust.

CHIPOTLE CHICKEN: In a skillet over medium-high, heat olive oil. Add shredded batch chicken and minced chipotle in adobo. Austin gets the full 1.5 tbsp — it should be punchy and smoky. Cameron gets just 1 tsp — taste hers separately. Toss to coat and cook 3–4 min until edges caramelize.
SPRING PICO: Mix quartered cherry tomatoes + minced spring onions + cilantro + lime juice + minced jalapeño (Austin only) + salt. Taste.
BUILD BOWLS: Rice base → chipotle chicken → black beans → spring pico → edamame if using.
Top with feta/cotija, a dollop of Greek yogurt, and a squeeze of lime.
Cameron gets 1/4 avocado sliced on top. Austin gets extra jalapeño and hot sauce.
Serve immediately. These bowls reheat well if needed — store components separately and assemble day-of.
recipes.batch_note: Chicken from batch — just toss in chipotle adobo and heat Friday night. Rice from batch. Spring pico made fresh.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: 1 tsp chipotle ONLY (not 1.5 tbsp — huge difference). Add 1/4 avocado on top. Extra lime squeeze.
recipes.seasonal_note: Spring onions in the pico instead of regular white onion — lighter, more aromatic, right for the season.

recipes.name: Smoked Spatchcock Chicken with Charred Snap Peas & Herb Chimichurri
recipes.serving_note: 1 whole chicken serves 2 for dinner + leftover for Sunday lunch
recipes.equipment: Smoker (apple wood), kitchen shears, wire rack + sheet pan, thermometer

ingredients.name: HERB CHIMICHURRI (double batch — baste + sauce + Sunday dressing)

instructions: FRIDAY NIGHT — SPATCHCOCK + DRY BRINE (10 min): Place chicken breast-side down on a cutting board. Using sharp kitchen shears, cut firmly along both sides of the backbone and remove it (save for stock). Flip breast-side up. Place both hands on the breastbone and press firmly until you hear it crack — bird should now lay flat. Mix dry brine rub and apply ALL OVER: under the breast skin, inside cavity, over the outside. Place on wire rack over sheet pan. Refrigerate uncovered overnight — this is key for crispy skin.

SATURDAY MORNING — MAKE CHIMICHURRI (10 min): Blend parsley + oregano + garlic + olive oil + red wine vinegar + red pepper flakes + salt. Pulse — keep it textured, not smooth. Taste and adjust. Jar it. Use half for basting, reserve half for serving + Sunday salad dressing.

SATURDAY — FIRE SMOKER (9–10am): Load smoker with apple wood chips. Heat to 275°F. Pull chicken from fridge 30 min before smoking. Place spatchcocked chicken skin-side UP directly on the grate. Insert thermometer probe into the thickest part of the breast.

SMOKE 2.5–3 hrs: Baste with chimichurri every 45–60 minutes. Target internal breast temp = 160°F (it will rise to 165°F during rest). Spatchcocked chicken cooks significantly faster than whole — start checking at 2 hrs.
REST + CARVE: Pull at 165°F. Tent loosely with foil and rest 10–15 min. Carve: legs/thighs for dinner, one breast for dinner, one breast + some thigh meat set aside for Sunday lunch salad.

CHARRED SIDES: While chicken rests, toss snap peas and asparagus with olive oil, salt, pepper. Char directly on grill grates or in a hot cast iron skillet 4–5 min — you want real color, not just warm.
PLATE: Carved smoked chicken with chimichurri spooned over top. Charred snap peas and asparagus alongside. Serve with extra chimichurri on the side for dipping.
recipes.batch_note: Dry brine Friday night. Fire smoker Saturday 9–10am for ~2.5 hr cook. Chimichurri made Saturday morning while smoker heats. Carve 1/3 bird for Sunday lunch leftovers.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: same plate, slightly smaller portion. The chimichurri is herb-forward not spicy — works perfectly for her.
recipes.seasonal_note: Spatchcocking cuts cook time vs. whole bird, keeps the smoke penetrating evenly. Spring snap peas and asparagus charred alongside round this out perfectly.

recipes.name: Smoked Chicken & Watercress Salad with Snap Peas, Radish & Chimichurri Vinaigrette
recipes.equipment: Large mixing bowl

ingredients.name: Saturday smoked spatchcock chicken, carved — breast + thigh

instructions: This is Sunday's no-cook lunch — it all comes from Saturday's smoker leftovers and batch chimichurri.
Carve reserved smoked chicken into bite-size pieces or slices. Serve at room temp or cold straight from the fridge — smoked chicken is excellent cold.
Toss watercress and arugula with leftover chimichurri (thin with a little extra lemon juice if the chimichurri has thickened overnight).
Add snap peas, radishes, and cherry tomatoes. Toss gently.
Pile dressed greens onto plates or into bowls. Top with smoked chicken.
Cameron adds 1/4 avocado sliced on top. Finish with flaky sea salt and cracked pepper.
The smokiness of the chicken is the star — keep the dressing light and let it shine.
recipes.batch_note: All from Saturday smoker leftovers and batch chimichurri. Sunday lunch is essentially free — 10 min assembly.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: add 1/4 avocado sliced on top. Extra lemon on the side. The chimichurri doubles as dressing.
recipes.seasonal_note: Watercress has a peppery bite that complements the smokiness of the chicken perfectly. Don't substitute arugula if watercress is available.

recipes.name: Spiced Shakshuka with Merguez Sausage, Feta & Warm Pita
recipes.equipment: Large oven-safe skillet or Le Creuset casserole dish, oven
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Le Creuset over medium-high. Add merguez sausage (removed from casing). Break apart and cook 5–6 min until browned and caramelized. Do not drain — the fat is flavor.
Add diced bell peppers and spring onions. Cook 3 min, stirring occasionally.
Add garlic and all spices (cumin, smoked paprika, cinnamon, red pepper flakes). Austin's pan gets cayenne + extra red pepper flakes. Stir 60 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes + diced fresh tomatoes. Stir to combine. Bring to a simmer and cook 8–10 min until sauce thickens and deepens in color. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Make 4 wells in the sauce using the back of a spoon — 2 for Austin, 2 for Cameron. Crack one egg into each well. Season egg tops with salt.
Transfer skillet to oven. Bake 8–12 min — check at 8 min. You want whites set but yolks still runny. Pull slightly early as they'll continue cooking in the hot pan.
Remove from oven. Immediately scatter feta and fresh cilantro over top.
Warm pita in a dry skillet 30 seconds per side.
Serve directly from the skillet. Cameron gets Greek yogurt dolloped on her portion and 1/4 avocado fanned on top. Austin gets extra hot sauce. Pita goes alongside for scooping.
recipes.batch_note: Cook to order Sunday night. One-pan meal in Le Creuset — 35 min start to finish. Easy batch-day dinner.
recipes.cameron_note: Cameron: pinch of red pepper flakes only, no cayenne. Add Greek yogurt dollop and 1/4 avocado on her portion. Mild-medium heat.
recipes.seasonal_note: Merguez sausage adds lamb + spice depth you don't get from regular sausage. Worth seeking out at a Middle Eastern market or Whole Foods.
